title: Your keys, your dragons
takeaway: Your seed phrase goes only into your own wallet, and nobody real will ever ask for it.

cards.title: A helper with a fix
cards.body: You post in the chat that your wallet shows the wrong balance. A minute later, a friendly account replies with a link to sync your wallet. The page looks clean and calm. It asks for your 12 words. Look at it closely before you do anything.

cards.title: What the seed phrase is
cards.body: Your seed phrase is 12 or 24 words. Whoever has those words owns your wallet, on any device. There is no password reset and no bank to call. You only type it when you restore your own wallet, in your own wallet app, on your own device.
points: A private key is just as secret. Never share it.

cards.title: Where people lose it
cards.body: Scammers rarely guess your words. They trick you into giving them away, or find a copy. Fake support sends you to sync, validate or restore pages. Malware and hacked cloud accounts expose photos, screenshots and notes. Keep your phrase on paper or metal, offline, where only you can reach it.
points: Never photograph, screenshot or read them out on a call.

cards.title: Try it
cards.body: This support chat looks friendly. Tap every red flag, then tap Done flagging.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting is normal. It proves nothing either way.

seg.label: Sync claim
seg.why: Wallets never need syncing through a stranger's link.

seg.label: Sync site link
seg.why: A site sent by a stranger in a DM.

seg.label: Request for seed phrase
seg.why: Nobody real ever asks for your seed phrase.

questions.stem: A mod DMs you: the raffle needs your seed phrase to confirm your wallet. What do you do?
options: Refuse, then block and report the account
Send only the first six words to confirm
Check their mod role in the server first
Type the words on the raffle site instead
questions.why: No real mod, team or app ever asks for your seed phrase, or any part of it. Block and report the account.

questions.stem: Your new wallet asks you to back up your seed phrase. Where do you keep it?
options: On paper, kept offline in a private place
In a password manager synced to the cloud
A photo in a hidden, locked phone album
In a note sent to your own email
questions.why: Photos, cloud notes and chats can be reached by malware or a hacked account. Paper kept offline cannot be scanned.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Greeting
seg.why: A greeting alone is not the problem.

seg.t: Your wallet failed our safety check.
seg.label: Fake problem
seg.why: An invented problem to scare you into acting.

seg.t: Type your recovery words here to restore it.
seg.label: Request for seed phrase
seg.why: Nobody real ever asks for your recovery words.

questions.why: A stranger invented a problem, then asked for your recovery words. Real support never needs your seed phrase. Block and report.

questions.stem: A site says your wallet is out of sync and asks you to restore it with your words. What is it?
options: A scam built to steal your wallet
A normal step after an update
A real check from your wallet's support team
A bug you can fix by trying again
questions.why: Wallets do not sync or validate through websites. Any site that wants your words is built to take your wallet.

questions.stem: On a video call, a support agent asks you to read your words aloud to check them. What do you do?
options: End the call, they never need your words
Read only the last few words to check
Share them only after they show a staff ID
Type them in the chat so nobody overhears
questions.why: Saying your words aloud gives them away, just like typing them. Real support never needs your seed phrase.

questions.stem: Who can take everything in your wallet?
options: Anyone who has your seed phrase
Anyone who knows your wallet address
Anyone who can see your NFTs
Only the company that made the app
questions.why: Your address is public and fine to share. Your seed phrase is the master key: whoever has it controls the wallet.

questions.stem: Tap the red flags in the web address, then Done.

url.label: Secure prefix
url.why: https only means the link is encrypted, not honest.

url.label: Validate domain
url.why: Wallets are never validated on a website.

page.title: Validate your wallet
lines: Enter your 12 words to keep your dragons.

questions.why: No website can validate a wallet. A page that asks for your 12 words is a trap, even with https in the address.

questions.stem: You find an old screenshot of your seed phrase in your gallery. What is the best move?
options: New wallet, move funds, then delete the photo
Delete the photo and empty the trash folder
Keep it, the phone has a strong lock
Move it to a hidden, locked cloud album
questions.why: The photo may already sit in a cloud backup. A fresh wallet with a new phrase written on paper removes that risk.

questions.stem: Tap every red flag, then Done.

seg.label: Thanks
seg.why: Friendly words are normal and prove nothing.

seg.t: To add you to the list,
seg.label: List mention
seg.why: Talking about a list is not the problem.

seg.label: Request for seed phrase
seg.why: No list ever needs your seed phrase.

seg.label: Time pressure
seg.why: A rush is there to stop you checking.

questions.why: A team name and badge are easy to copy. Asking for your seed phrase, with a rush, is always a scam.

questions.stem: A help site says it needs your private key, not your words, to fix a stuck mint. What do you do?
options: Refuse, a private key also controls your wallet
Share it, since it is not the seed
Share it only if the site uses https
Share it only with the site's verified admin
questions.why: A private key controls the account just like the seed phrase. Never share either one, in any form.
